proposals.name: Harrison Community Schools Operating Millage Renewal Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy 17.4362 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, and renews millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 17.4362 mills ($17.4362 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Harrison Community Schools,…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy 17.4362 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, and renews millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 17.4362 mills ($17.4362 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Harrison Community Schools, Clare and Gladwin Counties, Michigan, be renewed for a period of 10 years, 2027 to 2036, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 17.4362 mills are levied in 2027 is approximately $5,731,000 (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: Harrison Community Schools Operating Millage Renewal Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 17.4362 mills for 10 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.name: Mid Michigan College Charter Millage Proposal
proposals.description: Permanently restores 0.2929 mill of Mid Michigan College's Headlee-reduced charter millage (~$1.3M in 2027).
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal would restore Mid Michigan College's original millage, which has been reduced by the Headlee Amendment, and allow the college to levy on all taxable property the millage previously approved by the voters of the community college district.
Shall the limitation on the total amount of taxes which may be assessed against all taxable property within the community college district of Mid Michigan College, Michigan, be increased by 0.2929 mill ($0.2929 on each $1,000 of taxable value) in perpetuity to provide funds for all authorized charter millage purposes specified within the power of the college’s board of trustees; the estimate of the revenue the college will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $1,307,848 from the local taxes authorized in this proposal?
proposals.officialTitle: MID MICHIGAN COLLEGE CHARTER MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 0.2929 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.
proposals.taxImpact: About $29/year per $100,000 of taxable value — permanent.

proposals.name: Mid Michigan College Charter Millage Proposal
proposals.description: Permanently restores 0.2929 mill of Mid Michigan College's Headlee-reduced charter millage (~$1.3M in 2027).
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal would restore Mid Michigan College's original millage, which has been reduced by the Headlee Amendment, and allow the college to levy on all taxable property the millage previously approved by the voters of the community college district.
Shall the limitation on the total amount of taxes which may be assessed against all taxable property within the community college district of Mid Michigan College, Michigan, be increased by 0.2929 mill ($0.2929 on each $1,000 of taxable value) in perpetuity to provide funds for all authorized charter millage purposes specified within the power of the college’s board of trustees; the estimate of the revenue the college will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $1,307,848 from the local taxes authorized in this proposal?
proposals.officialTitle: MID MICHIGAN COLLEGE CHARTER MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 0.2929 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.
proposals.taxImpact: About $29/year per $100,000 of taxable value — permanent.
